The '''Eagles–Giants rivalry''' is a [[National Football League]] (NFL) [[List of NFL rivalries|rivalry]] between the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] and [[New York Giants]].

The rivalry began in 1933 with the founding of the Eagles, and slowly strengthened when both teams came to relative prominence in the 1940s and 1950s. The two teams have played in the same division in the NFL every year since 1933, making it the second-oldest rivalry in the [[NFC East]] division, behind only New York's [[Commanders-Giants rivalry|rivalry]] with the [[Washington Commanders]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Eagles-Giants rivalry goes back a long time |url=https://www.berkshireeagle.com/sports/local_sports/eagles-giants-rivalry-goes-back-a-long-time/article_9b14fedd-7c43-5ef6-8b6c-efb66087e8b4.html |access-date=June 22, 2022 |website=The Berkshire Eagle |language=en}}</ref> The ferocity of the rivalry can also be attributed to the geographic [[Sports in New York City|New York]]-[[Sports in Philadelphia|Philadelphia]] rivalry, which is mirrored in [[Major League Baseball]]'s [[Mets–Phillies rivalry]] and the [[National Hockey League]]'s [[Flyers–Rangers rivalry]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Stolnis |first=John |date=December 6, 2019 |title=NFC East futility has destroyed the traditional rivalries |url=https://www.bleedinggreennation.com/2019/12/6/20998560/nfc-east-futility-destroyed-traditional-division-rivalries-eagles-cowboys-giants-redskins-2019-teams |access-date=June 22, 2022 |website=Bleeding Green Nation |language=en}}</ref> It is ranked by [[NFL Network]] as the number one rivalry of all-time<ref>{{Cite magazine |title=The History of the Giants–Eagles Rivalry |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/The-History-of-the-Giants-Eagles-Rivalry |access-date=2024-03-04 |magazine=Sports Illustrated |language=en-us}}</ref> and ''Sports Illustrated'' ranks it amongst the top ten NFL rivalries of all-time at number four,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/multimedia/photo_gallery/2005/12/15/gallery.oldrivals/content.7.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20051217181045/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/multimedia/photo_gallery/2005/12/15/gallery.oldrivals/content.7.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 17, 2005|title=Top 10 NFL Rivalries Of All Time: No. 4 Giants-Eagles|publisher=si.com}}</ref> and according to [[ESPN]], it is one of the fiercest and most well-known rivalries in the football community.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/columns/story?columnist=chadiha_jeffri&id=3086647|title=Ranking the NFL's best rivalries: Where does Colts-Pats fit? |last=Chadiha |first=Jeffri |work=ESPN.com |date=October 31, 2007 |access-date=April 12, 2008}}</ref>

The Eagles lead the overall series, 97–90–2. The two teams have met five times in the [[National Football League playoffs|playoffs]], with the Eagles holding a 3–2 advantage.<ref name="Head2Head"/>

== Notable rivalry moments ==
===The Hit: 1960===
{{Main article|The Hit (Chuck Bednarik)}}
In a November 20, 1960, game, the [[1960 Philadelphia Eagles season|Eagles]]' [[Chuck Bednarik]] cleanly blindsided [[1960 New York Giants season|Giants]] running back [[Frank Gifford]] in a play known as [[The Hit (Chuck Bednarik)|The Hit]], widely considered the hardest, or one of the hardest, tackles in the history of the [[National Football League]] that sent Gifford to the ground unconscious. He was removed from the field by stretcher, transported to a hospital by ambulance, and diagnosed with a severe concussion. The play forced Gifford out of the game for 18 months before he was ultimately able to return with the Giants.<ref name=BestRivalry>{{cite news|title=The Birds' Biggest Rival—In a division of fierce foes, the Giants have battled the Eagles as tough as anyone|date=September 17, 2006|first=Bob|last=Brookover|newspaper=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]|page=D1}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Burke|first=Garrett|title=The Facts and Fiction Behind Chuck Bednarik's Hit on Wide Receiver Frank Gifford|url=https://www.sportscasting.com/the-facts-and-fiction-behind-chuck-bednariks-hit-on-wide-receiver-frank-gifford/|website=Sportscasting.com|date=June 8, 2020|access-date=September 27, 2022}}</ref>

===The Miracle at the Meadowlands/The Fumble: 1978===
{{Main article|Miracle at the Meadowlands}}
On November 19, 1978, at Giants Stadium, the [[1978 New York Giants season|Giants]] were leading the [[1978 Philadelphia Eagles season|Eagles]] 17–12 with 20 seconds remaining. Offensive coordinator [[Bob Gibson (American football)|Bob Gibson]] called for a running play when all that was needed was for the Giants to take a knee having previously got run over while kneeling the very prior play. The handoff between quarterback [[Joe Pisarcik]] and [[Larry Csonka]] was fumbled and Eagles cornerback [[Herman Edwards]] grabbed the loose ball and returned it for the winning score.<ref>{{YouTube|title=1978 NFL Philadelphia at NY Giants 11-19-1978|id=pQRRPwRdWwA}}</ref><ref>{{YouTube|title=#3 Miracle at the Meadowlands {{!}} NFL Films {{!}} Top 10 Worst Plays|id=hfOiY5MhqHA}}</ref> This play is commonly referred to as [[Miracle at the Meadowlands|The Miracle at the Meadowlands]] by Eagles fans and just "The Fumble" by Giants fans.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Katz |first=Michael |author-link=Michael Katz (journalist) |date=November 20, 1978 |title=Giants Voice Mutual Animosity |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1978/11/19/archives/giants-voice-mutual-animosity-a-natural-leader-third-and-long-run.html |access-date=February 13, 2024 |website=[[New York Times]] |page=S3}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Katz |first=Michael |author-link=Michael Katz (journalist) |date=November 21, 1978 |title=Giants Oust Gibson A Day After Bungle |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1978/11/21/archives/giants-oust-gibson-a-day-after-bungle-giants-oust-gibson-a-day.html |access-date=February 13, 2024 |website=[[New York Times]] |page=C19}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Anderson |first=Dave |author-link=Dave Anderson (sportswriter) |date=December 3, 1978 |title=Fanning the Fire at Giants Stadium |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1978/12/03/archives/fanning-the-fire-at-giants-stadium-sports-of-the-times.html |access-date=February 13, 2024 |website=[[New York Times]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Anderson |first=Dave |author-link=Dave Anderson (sportswriter) |date=December 11, 1978 |title=The Fans' Sign From the Sky |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1978/12/11/archives/the-fans-sign-from-the-sky.html |access-date=February 13, 2024 |website=[[New York Times]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Branch |first=John |author-link=John Branch (journalist) |date=February 2, 2015 |title=How One Bad Giants Call Ended an N.F.L. Career |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2015/02/03/sports/football/how-one-bad-giants-call-ended-an-nfl-career.html |access-date=February 13, 2024 |website=[[New York Times]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Pumerantz |first=Zack |title=The 50 Worst Screw-Ups in Sports History |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1265467-the-50-worst-screw-ups-in-sports-history |access-date=2024-02-13 |website=Bleacher Report |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Hank |first=Gola |date=2008-11-18 |title=30 years later, Giant disappointment of 'The Fumble' still lingers |url=https://www.nydailynews.com/2008/11/18/30-years-later-giant-disappointment-of-the-fumble-still-lingers/ |access-date=2024-02-13 |website=New York Daily News |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Ellenport |first=Craig |date=2018-11-14 |title=Miracle at the Meadowlands: The fumble that changed football |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/2018/11/14/miracle-meadowlands-40th-anniversary-giants-eagles-joe-pisarcik-herman-edwards-harry-carson |access-date=2024-02-13 |magazine=Sports Illustrated |language=en-us}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Papale |first=Vince |date=2013-11-20 |title=The Miracle at the Meadowlands: 35 years later, I (still) don't believe it! |url=https://www.inquirer.com/philly/columnists/vince_papale/The_Miracle_at_the_Meadowlands_35_years_later_I_still_dont_believe_it.html |access-date=2024-02-13 |website=[[Philadelphia Inquirer]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Morgan |first=Craig |title=Herm Edwards looks back — and breaks news — on 40-year-old Miracle at the Meadowlands |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/656769/2018/11/15/herm-edwards-looks-back-and-breaks-news-on-40-year-old-miracle-at-the-meadowlands/ |access-date=2024-02-13 |website=The Athletic |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Werner |first=Barry |title=45 years ago: Herman Edwards and the Miracle at the Meadowlands happened |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/2023/11/19/45-years-ago-herman-edwards-and-the-miracle-at-the-meadowlands-happened/71645974007/ |access-date=2024-02-13 |website=USA TODAY |language=en-US}}</ref>

===1981 NFC wild card game===
{{unsourced section|date=January 2024}}
In 1981, both the [[1981 New York Giants season|Giants]] and the defending NFC champion [[1981 Philadelphia Eagles season|Eagles]] qualified for playoff berths. The Eagles hosted the Giants on December 27 in a wild card game. The Giants, led by quarterback [[Scott Brunner]] and head coach [[Ray Perkins (wide receiver)|Ray Perkins]], took a 20–0 lead in the first quarter. The Eagles rallied but never led and the Giants held on to win 27–21. The game ended with Scott Brunner kneeling down on the ball, which was revenge for the Joe Pisarcik game some three years earlier. The Giants would go on to lose 38–24 to the [[1981 San Francisco 49ers season|San Francisco 49ers]], the eventual [[Super Bowl XVI]] champions.

===1988 division title===
The [[1988 NFL season]] saw both teams competing for the NFC East title. On November 20, 1988, the [[1988 New York Giants season|Giants]] hosted the [[1988 Philadelphia Eagles season|Eagles]] with both teams in the running for control over their division. The Eagles, led by head coach [[Buddy Ryan]] and quarterback [[Randall Cunningham]], fought a tough match to bring the game into overtime with the score tied at 17–17. In overtime, Eagles defensive lineman [[Clyde Simmons]] carried the ball 15 yards after a blocked Eagles field goal attempt for the game-winning touchdown, completing a season sweep of the Giants. This was dubbed the "Forgotten Miracle at the Meadowlands."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Devlin |first=Pat |date=2020-11-13 |title=Remembering the Eagles' forgotten Miracle at the Meadowlands |url=https://www.nbcsportsphiladelphia.com/nfl/philadelphia-eagles/remembering-the-eagles-forgotten-miracle-at-the-meadowlands/172867/ |access-date=2024-02-13 |website=NBC Sports Philadelphia |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{YouTube|title=Miracle at the meadowlands number 2|id=_JnCdrj3yBI}}</ref> Both teams finished with 10–6 records, but the Eagles won the NFC East due to their head-to-head victories, while the Giants lost the wild card tiebreaker to the [[1988 Los Angeles Rams season|Los Angeles Rams]] and missed the playoffs. The Eagles would lose to the [[1988 Chicago Bears season|Chicago Bears]] in a game famously known as the [[Fog Bowl (American football)|Fog Bowl]].<ref>{{cite web|author=SI Staff|title=Pinnacle Moments in NFL History|url=https://www.si.com/nfl/2010/09/08/08pinnacle-moments-in-nfl-history|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=September 8, 2010|access-date=December 10, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=August 19, 2009 |title=Top 10 weather games in NFL history |url=https://www.nfl.com/nflnetwork/story/09000d5d80870a4e/article/top-10-weather-games-in-nfl-history |access-date=2012-08-09 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

===2000 NFC divisional game===
{{unsourced section|date=January 2024}}
On January 7, 2001, the [[2000 New York Giants season|Giants]] defeated the [[2000 Philadelphia Eagles season|Eagles]] 20–10 in a divisional playoff game with the help of Ron Dixon's 97-yard kickoff return and [[Jason Sehorn]]'s acrobatic 32-yard interception return. This win helped propel the Giants to [[Super Bowl XXXV]], which they lost to the [[2000 Baltimore Ravens season|Baltimore Ravens]], 34–7.

===2006 NFC wild card game===
{{unsourced section|date=January 2024}}
On January 7, 2007, the [[2006 Philadelphia Eagles season|Eagles]] defeated the [[2006 New York Giants season|Giants]] 23–20 in a wild card playoff game on a [[David Akers]] field goal as time expired. The Eagles had relinquished a ten-point lead in the fourth quarter, with the Giants tying the game on a touchdown by [[Plaxico Burress]] with just over five minutes remaining. [[Jeff Garcia]] and [[Brian Westbrook]] led the game-winning drive deep into Giants territory, allowing the Eagles to drain the clock to three seconds before Akers lined up his 38-yard kick to win the game.

===2008 NFC Divisional Game===
{{unsourced section|date=January 2024}}
The two teams split their 2008 meetings. The [[2008 New York Giants season|Giants]] rallied to edge the [[2008 Philadelphia Eagles season|Eagles]] in Philadelphia 36–31, then the Eagles stymied New York's offense en route to a 20–14 win at Giants Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey. They met again at Giants Stadium on January 11, 2009, in the 2008 NFC Divisional Playoffs. In what would ultimately be the final playoff game at the venue, the #6 seeded Eagles defeated the top-seeded Giants 23–11, leaving the series tied 2–2 in the all-time playoff series.

===Miracle at the New Meadowlands: 2010===
{{Main article|Miracle at the New Meadowlands}}
On [[Miracle at the New Meadowlands|December 19, 2010]], the [[2010 New York Giants season|Giants]] led the [[2010 Philadelphia Eagles season|Eagles]] 31–10 with 7:28 left in the first game between the teams at [[New Meadowlands Stadium]] where first place in the NFC East was on the line. But the Eagles rallied to tie the score and then won the game on [[DeSean Jackson]]'s 65 yard punt return for a touchdown with no time left on the clock for a 38–31 victory.<ref name=NewMeadowlands>{{cite news|title=Miracle at the Meadowlands — Comeback, runback give Birds their East edge back|date=December 20, 2010|first=Jeff|last=McLane|newspaper=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]|page=D1}}</ref> The [[Elias Sports Bureau]] noted that this is the first walk-off punt return in NFL history.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/Story.asp?story_id=22937|title=The First Walk-Off Punt Return In History?|work=www.philadelphiaeagles.com|date=December 19, 2010|first=Chris|last=McPhersonm|access-date=December 20, 2010|archive-date=December 24, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101224024336/http://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/Story.asp?story_id=22937|url-status=dead}}</ref> The Giants missed the playoffs, despite finishing tied for first with the Eagles at 10–6,<ref name=2010Season>{{cite news|title=Giants beat Redskins 17-14, but miss playoffs|date=January 2, 2011|first=Howard|last=Fendrich|agency=Associated Press|quote=The Giants (10-6) and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers are the first NFC teams since 1991 to miss out on the postseason despite double-digit victory totals.}}</ref> and the Eagles lost their last two games.<ref>{{cite news|title=Pack Coming Back—Eagles fall to Cowboys, start preparing for rematch with Green Bay|date=January 3, 2011|first=Jeff|last=McLane|newspaper=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]|page=E1}}</ref>

===Other notable moments===
*On December 18, 1994, the [[1994 New York Giants season|Giants]] beat the [[1994 Philadelphia Eagles season|Eagles]] at Veterans Stadium, giving them their fifth consecutive win after starting 3–7, while giving the Eagles their sixth consecutive loss of the season after a 7–2 start. This led to the firing of Philadelphia's then-head coach [[Rich Kotite]] after the season's conclusion.
* On October 31, 1999, at Veterans Stadium in overtime, [[1999 Philadelphia Eagles season|Eagles]]' quarterback (and future head coach) [[Doug Pederson]] had his pass blocked up in the air and was intercepted by [[Michael Strahan]] and returned for a 44-yard touchdown to win the game for the [[1999 New York Giants season|Giants]] 23–17.
* In Week 6 of the 2001 season, the [[2001 Philadelphia Eagles season|Eagles]] broke a nine-game losing streak against the [[2001 New York Giants season|Giants]]. James Thrash caught the winning touchdown from Donovan McNabb in the fourth quarter.
* In week 2 of the 2006 season, the [[2006 New York Giants season|Giants]] met the [[2006 Philadelphia Eagles season|Eagles]] in Philadelphia and were down 24–7 by the end of the 3rd quarter. In the 4th quarter of regulation the Giants responded with two more touchdowns and a field goal to tie the game 24–24 and go into overtime. In overtime the Giants defeated the Eagles when quarterback [[Eli Manning]] threw a 31-yard pass to Plaxico Burress.
* On September 30, 2007, the [[2007 New York Giants season|Giants]] sacked [[2007 Philadelphia Eagles season|Eagles]] quarterback [[Donovan McNabb]] 12 times (tying an NFL record) en route to a 16–3 win. New York's defense held the Eagles scoreless in the first half, while in the second quarter, New York got on the board first with quarterback Eli Manning completing a 9-yard touchdown pass to wide receiver Plaxico Burress. In the third quarter, the Giants increased their lead with kicker Lawrence Tynes getting a 29-yard field goal, along with linebacker Kawika Mitchell returning a fumble 17-yards for a touchdown. In the fourth quarter, the Eagles would get their only points of the game with kicker David Akers making a 53-yard field goal. Later that year, [[2007-08 NFL playoffs|in the 2007 playoffs]], New York would go on to defeat the [[2007 New England Patriots season|18–0 unbeaten New England Patriots]] in [[Super Bowl XLII]].
* On October 12, 2014, the [[2014 Philadelphia Eagles season|Eagles]] authored their first shutout win in the series since [[1996 Philadelphia Eagles season|1996]], winning 27–0.  Quarterback [[Nick Foles]] threw for 248 yards and two touchdowns while he and three Eagles running backs rushed for 203 yards, led by [[LeSean McCoy]]'s 149 yards.  The [[2014 New York Giants season|Giants]] failed on a fourth and goal attempt in the third quarter following a Foles interception; even worse, wide receiver [[Victor Cruz (American football)|Victor Cruz]] suffered a season-ending injury on the play. (This led to an off-field episode in the rivalry, as the cover of the next morning's ''[[New York Daily News]]'' showed a cheering Eagles employee and the fallen Cruz under the headline "PHILTHY!", implying that the man was celebrating the injury rather than the result of the play. However, this photo was later debunked as being taken out of context.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sbnation.com/lookit/2014/10/13/6969247/new-york-daily-news-cover-eagles-giants-victor-cruz-injury-cheering|title= New York newspaper wants you to believe the Eagles cheered Victor Cruz's injury |work=SB Nation|date=October 13, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://ftw.usatoday.com/2014/10/eagles-fans-cheer-victor-cruz-injury-new-york-daily-news-headline|title=Eagles fans didn't 'gloat' over Victor Cruz's injury, despite what NY tabloid says|work=USA Today|date=October 13, 2014}}</ref>)  [[Eli Manning]] was held to 151 yards and backup [[Ryan Nassib]] connected for 60 yards.
* On September 24, 2017, in Philadelphia, kicker [[Jake Elliott]] kicked a 61-yard field goal to beat the [[2017 New York Giants season|New York Giants]] with no time on the clock for the final play of the game, resulting in a 27–24 victory. Previously regarded as nothing more than a replacement kicker for injured [[Caleb Sturgis]], the kick earned Elliott NFC Special Teams Player of the Week honors, cementing him as a strong kicking option for the [[2017 Philadelphia Eagles season|2017 Eagles]]. Elliott's kick set an Eagles' franchise record for the longest field goal, tied for the 7th-longest field goal in NFL history, and was the longest since November 2015. Elliott helped the Eagles to their first Super Bowl victory later that season in [[Super Bowl LII]].
* On December 9, 2019, an ankle injury previously suffered by [[2019 New York Giants season|Giants]] quarterback [[Daniel Jones (American football)|Daniel Jones]] would result in Eli Manning returning to the starting lineup against the [[2019 Philadelphia Eagles season|Eagles]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lombardo |first=Matt |date=December 4, 2019 |title=Eli Manning expected to start vs. Packers; Giants QB Daniel Jones injured |url=https://syracuse.com/sports/2019/12/eli-manning-expected-to-start-vs-packers-giants-qb-daniel-jones-injured.html |access-date=December 11, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191217162127/https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401128013 |archive-date=December 17, 2019 |access-date=December 9, 2019 |website=[[ESPN]] |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> Manning retired at the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Duggan |first=Dan |date=December 10, 2019 |title=Tale of two halves: Eli Manning's likely final |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210921203929/https://theathletic.com/1448109/2019/12/10/eli-manning-loses-again-to-the-eagles-possibly-for-the-last-time/ |archive-date=September 21, 2021 |access-date=September 21, 2021 |website=[[The Athletic]]}}</ref>
*On January 3, 2021, with the [[2020 New York Giants season|Giants]] having won earlier in the day, they needed the [[2020 Philadelphia Eagles season|Eagles]], who were eliminated from playoff contention, to defeat the [[2020 Washington Football Team season|Washington Football Team]] in order to for the Giants to clinch the NFC East division. The Eagles lost to Washington; Washington rallied from down 14–10 to win 20–14 thus giving them the [[NFC East]] title and eliminating the Giants from the playoffs. Eagles head coach [[Doug Pederson]] was criticized for benching struggling rookie [[Jalen Hurts]] and was questioned in some media circles on how hard his team played. The loss advanced the Eagles three spots in the 2021 NFL Draft to sixth.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nbcphiladelphia.com/news/sports/eagles/giants-players-lose-it-over-eagles-qb-switch-vs-washington/2654065/|title = Giants Players Lose It Over Eagles' QB Switch Vs. Washington| date=January 4, 2021 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.inquirer.com/eagles/philadelphia-eagles-lose-20-14-week-17-washington-carson-wentz-jalen-hurts-20210103.html|title=Eagles successfully lose, 20–14, despite Washington's poor effort; Birds will draft sixth overall after 4–11–1 season|date=January 3, 2021 }}</ref> Giants running back [[Saquon Barkley]] would tweet his disbelief at what was happening, to which former Giants quarterback Eli Manning would reply "This is why we don't like the Eagles."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Davis |first=Scott |date=January 4, 2021 |url=https://www.yahoo.com/news/eli-manning-said-why-dont-151627389.html|title=Eli Manning said 'This is why we don't like the Eagles' after a bizarre coaching decision spoiled the Giants' playoff hopes |access-date=February 11, 2025 |website=[[Yahoo!]]}}</ref>
*On March 26, 2021, after it was alleged that the [[2021 Philadelphia Eagles season|Eagles]] tanked in their week 17 game to moved up three spots in the draft, the Eagles traded with the [[2021 Miami Dolphins season|Dolphins]] to move down to the 12th overall pick.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/2021-nfl-draft-eagles-trade-no-6-pick-to-dolphins-receive-no-12-pick-and-2022-first-round-pick-in-return/|title = 2021 NFL Draft: Eagles trade No. 6 pick to Dolphins, receive No. 12 pick and 2022 first-round pick in return| date=March 26, 2021 }}</ref> While the Eagles gained a 2022 first-round pick from the trade, this made many [[2021 New York Giants season|Giants]] fans angry since trading back seemingly removed any good reason for the Eagles to have tanked in week 17 in spite of any leverage gained from the higher draft position contributing to the trade being completed. Leading up to the [[2021 NFL draft]], the Giants were sitting at 11th overall. As the draft went on, it was suspected that the Giants would draft wide receiver and 2020 Heisman Trophy winner [[DeVonta Smith]]. However, the Eagles traded in-division with [[2021 Dallas Cowboys season|Dallas]] to move up to the 10th overall pick and drafted Smith, which reportedly made the Giants front office "livid.”<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/giants-reportedly-livid-eagles-traded-up-ahead-of-them-to-select-devonta-smith-at-2021-nfl-draft/|title=Giants reportedly livid Eagles traded up ahead of them to select DeVonta Smith at 2021 NFL Draft|date=May 7, 2021 }}</ref> The Eagles' trade-up resulted in the Giants trading down to the 20th pick with the [[2021 Chicago Bears season|Chicago Bears]], and they would select [[Florida Gators football|Florida]] wide receiver [[Kadarius Toney]].
*On March 11, 2024, [[2024 New York Giants season|Giants]] running back Saquon Barkley agreed to a 3-year, $37.75 million contract with the [[2024 Philadelphia Eagles season|Eagles]] after a six-year career with the Giants. The entire process was shown during a special offseason edition of [[HBO]] ''[[Hard Knocks (2001 TV series)|Hard Knocks]]'' where Giants general manager [[Joe Schoen]] had stated to Giants executives on camera that they were not "paying a $40 million quarterback (in reference to [[Daniel Jones (American football)|Daniel Jones]]) to hand off to a $12 million running back (in reference to Barkley)".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith  |first=Michael David |date=July 3, 2024 |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/joe-schoen-were-not-paying-daniel-jones-40-million-to-hand-off-to-a-12-million-back |title=Joe Schoen: We’re not paying Daniel Jones $40 million to hand off to a $12 million back |access-date=February 11, 2025 |website=[[NBC Sports]]}}</ref> Giants owner [[John Mara]] was also recorded saying that he "would have a hard time sleeping if Saquon goes to Philadelphia".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Traina  |first=Patricia |date=June 5, 2024 |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/giants-owner-quote-saquon-barkley-eagles-debut |title=Giants Owner's Quote About Saquon Barkley Resurfaced During Stellar Eagles Debut |access-date=February 11, 2025 |website=[[Sports Illustrated]]}}</ref> Eagles head coach [[Nick Sirianni]] would later tell reporters that during that offseason, if heckled badly by Giants fans, he would reply "you know, we got your best player".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Capurso |first=Tim |date=September 7, 2024 |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/giants/big-blue-plus/eagles-head-coach-nick-sirianni-gives-giants-fans-yet-another-reason-to-dislike-him-01hzjda36p1g |title=Eagles Head Coach Nick Sirianni Gives Giants Fans Yet Another Reason to Dislike Him |access-date=February 11, 2025 |website=[[Sports Illustrated]]}}</ref> On October 20, 2024 in his return to [[MetLife Stadium]], amidst a chorus of boos from his former fans, Barkley rushed for 176 yards and a touchdown in a 28–3 Eagles win. Jones was later benched and requested his release on November 22, 2024 which the Giants granted. Barkley ultimately became the 9th running back to join the [[2,000-yard club]], finishing with 2,005 rushing yards in 16 games, and the Eagles would win [[Super Bowl LIX]] that season.

== Rivalry outside football ==
* The 2006 film ''[[Invincible (2006 film)|Invincible]]'' follows [[Vince Papale]] ([[Mark Wahlberg]]) and his rise to playing for the Eagles. He crushes on a coworker, who, being from New York, is a Giants fan, and in his breakout game, the Eagles play the Giants when he recovers a muffed punt for a touchdown.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/29143543/bond-disney-invincible-strong|title=Mark Wahlberg, Vince Papale: Bond from Disney's 'Invincible' still strong|last=Reiss|first=Mike|publisher=ESPN Enterprises Inc.|date=May 8, 2020|website=ESPN.com|accessdate=June 3, 2024}}</ref>
* The 2009 film ''[[Big Fan]]'' depicts a Giants fan ([[Patton Oswalt]]) and his bitter rivalry with an Eagles fan ([[Michael Rapaport]]).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://slate.com/culture/2009/08/big-fan-will-be-a-cult-classic.html|title=Big Fan will be a cult classic|last=Stevens|first=Dana|publisher=The Slate Group|date=August 28, 2009|website=Slate.com|accessdate=June 3, 2024}}</ref>
* After winning the [[2022–23 NFL playoffs#NFC Championship Game: Philadelphia Eagles 31, San Francisco 49ers 7|NFC championship]] on January 29, 2023, the [[Empire State Building]] lit up to celebrate the Eagles making the Super Bowl. This sparked outrage from many people in New York, including mayor [[Eric Adams]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Benton |first=Dan |date=February 3, 2023 |title=Empire State Building plans to go green again if Eagles win Super Bowl |url=https://giantswire.usatoday.com/2023/02/03/empire-state-building-plans-to-go-green-again-if-philadelphia-eagles-win-super-bowl/ |access-date=February 4, 2023 |website=Giants Wire|publisher=USA Today}}</ref>
